items.stem: A platform's main pain is that eight teams constantly block each other in one large codebase. Which architectural goal most directly addresses this?

options.text: Clear module boundaries aligned to team ownership
options.rationale: Correct: boundaries aligned to ownership let teams work independently and reduce blocking.
More shared global state increases coupling and blocking, not less.

options.text: Rendering every page on the server
options.rationale: Rendering strategy does not resolve team coordination pain.
Removing shared components worsens consistency without helping autonomy.

items.explanation: Correct: boundaries aligned to ownership let teams work independently and reduce blocking.

items.stem: Which TWO are genuine costs of adopting micro-frontends? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Operational and integration complexity across independently deployed pieces
options.rationale: Correct: composing independently deployed frontends adds integration and operational overhead.

options.text: Risk of duplicated dependencies and larger total payload
options.rationale: Correct: independent bundles can duplicate shared libraries and inflate payload.

options.text: They eliminate all need for coordination between teams
options.rationale: Coordination is still required for shared contracts and shells.

options.text: They are always faster for end users
options.rationale: They can be slower due to duplication and composition cost; speed is not guaranteed.

items.explanation: Correct: composing independently deployed frontends adds integration and operational overhead.

items.stem: Course catalogue data is read on almost every page and changes rarely. Which strategy fits best?

options.text: Cache it with revalidation so reads are fast and occasional changes still propagate
options.rationale: Correct: caching read-heavy, rarely changing data with revalidation balances speed and freshness.

options.text: Refetch it from the server on every render
options.rationale: Refetching rarely changing data on every render wastes requests and slows pages.

options.text: Store it in per-component local state only
options.rationale: Local state cannot be shared efficiently across many pages.
Refusing to cache read-heavy stable data needlessly harms performance.

items.explanation: Correct: caching read-heavy, rarely changing data with revalidation balances speed and freshness.
